related_questions.question: How serious is catching COVID-19 now?
related_questions.snippet: Many people with COVID-19, also called coronavirus disease 2019, recover at home. But for some, COVID-19 can be a serious illness. Some people may need care in the hospital, treatment in the intensive care unit and the need for breathing help. In some people, severe COVID-19 illness can lead to death.
related_questions.title: COVID-19: Who's at higher risk of serious symptoms? - Mayo Clinic

text_blocks.snippet: To help COVID-19 symptoms resolve, focus on rest, hydration, and symptom management with over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen. For individuals at higher risk of severe illness, antiviral medications authorized or approved by the FDA can help prevent the virus from multiplying. Consult with a healthcare professional for personalized advice, especially if symptoms worsen or if you have underlying health conditions.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on rest, hydration, and symptom management with over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen

list.title: Rest and Hydration:
list.snippet: Getting enough rest allows your body to focus on fighting the virus, while staying hydrated helps with overall recovery.

list.title: Symptom Relief:
list.snippet: Over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) can help reduce fever and aches.

list.title: Antiviral Medications:
list.snippet: If you are at higher risk for severe COVID-19, your doctor may prescribe antiviral medications like Paxlovid to help stop the virus from multiplying in your body.

list.title: Isolation:
list.snippet: To prevent spreading the virus, stay home and away from others, especially those with weakened immune systems, while you are experiencing symptoms.

list.title: Consult a Doctor:
list.snippet: If your symptoms worsen or if you have underlying health conditions, consult with your doctor for further guidance and treatment options.
